body:
added 1 commit
  • 115b6d84 - Record phase 2 of the object save fixes: built, in review as MR !24
[Compare with previous version](/max757/Luminari-Source/-/merge_requests/24/diffs?diff_id=2077702172&start_sha=b06a2367fdb4f936af90dc248b4e65a61e781ae9)

**Finding 1 (data loss on a failure path): when the new permanent-table migration fails, the test overwrites `owner_id` on every permanent `pet_data` row**

**Location.** `unittests/CuTest/test_database_persistence.c:832-845` at `115b6d846`.

`fixture_created = live_tables_migrated && create_legacy_pet_temporary_schema(connection)` skips the temporary tables whenever the new first call returns false. Nothing below it stops. Line 842 runs `UPDATE pet_data SET owner_id = 4294967295` with no `WHERE` and no guard, and with no temporary `pet_data` in the session that name is the permanent table.

On base the statement could reach the permanent table only if a `CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE` failed. This MR puts in front of it a run of up to fifteen DDL statements on shared tables that fails in ordinary states; the description itself names one.

**Effect.** Every row of the configured database's `pet_data` ends with `owner_id = 4294967295`. `prepare_saved_pet_row()` (`src/player/players.c:7245`) refuses a row whose `owner_id` is neither 0 nor the owner's, and the pet queries at `players.c:7110`, `:7775`, `:7823` and `:7877` filter on the same pair, so no owner loads or reclaims those pets again. CI's disposable databases hold no pet rows, so nothing is lost there; the loss is on any database that does hold them. The sibling `Test_pet_live_schema_cascades_objects_and_rejects_orphans` keeps its row writes in a transaction it rolls back; this test now has no such protection.

**Repro.** mariadb:10.11, database built from `sql/master_schema.sql`, boot skipped, one pet row inserted with `owner_id = 7`. Three states that make the first call fail, each run on base `8c0c5bd16` and on head:

| State | Base | Head |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Key added to the permanent `pet_save_objs` by hand, nothing recorded (the plan's step 1 probe state) | passes; row keeps `owner_id` 7 | fails at `:873`, `Failed to apply migration 2026080503: Cannot change column 'pet_idnum': used in a foreign key constraint`; row has 4294967295 |
| Fully migrated database, test user granted only SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE TEMPORARY TABLES | fails at `:872`; row keeps 7 | fails at `:873`, `CREATE command denied ... schema_migrations`; row has 4294967295 |
| Two `./cutest` processes started together on one fresh database | not applicable, the test was session-private | 3 of 3 rounds: one process fails with `Failed to record migration 2026080501: Duplicate entry`; row has 4294967295 |

The first state, start to finish:

```bash
docker run -d --rm --name probe -p 127.0.0.24:3306:3306 -e MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD=probe \
  -e MARIADB_DATABASE=probe mariadb:10.11
docker exec -i probe mariadb -uroot -pprobe probe < sql/master_schema.sql
docker exec -i probe mariadb -uroot -pprobe probe <<'SQL'
INSERT INTO pet_data (owner_name, vnum, hp, max_hp, str, con, dex, level, ac, pet_name,
  pet_sdesc, pet_ldesc, pet_ddesc, owner_id, owner_created)
VALUES ('Realowner', 1, 10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 1, 10, 'rex', 'a dog', 'A dog.', 'dog', 7, 1700000000);
ALTER TABLE pet_save_objs ADD CONSTRAINT fk_pet_save_objs_pet FOREIGN KEY (pet_idnum)
  REFERENCES pet_data (pet_data_id) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE;
SQL
LUMINARI_TEST_MYSQL_ENABLE=1 LUMINARI_TEST_MYSQL_HOST=127.0.0.24 LUMINARI_TEST_MYSQL_PORT=3306 \
  LUMINARI_TEST_MYSQL_USER=root LUMINARI_TEST_MYSQL_PASSWORD=probe \
  LUMINARI_TEST_MYSQL_DATABASE=probe LUMINARI_TEST_SKIP_SYNTAX_BOOT=1 \
  CUTEST_FILTER=Test_pet_persistence_legacy_schema_migration_is_idempotent ./cutest
docker exec probe mariadb -uroot -pprobe probe -e "SELECT owner_name, owner_id FROM pet_data"
```

Head prints `Realowner 4294967295`; base prints `Realowner 7`.

**Fix.** Stop when the fixture is not in place. Everything below that point is written for the temporary tables.

```diff
   live_tables_migrated = run_pet_persistence_migrations();
   fixture_created = live_tables_migrated && create_legacy_pet_temporary_schema(connection);
-  first_migration = fixture_created && run_pet_persistence_migrations();
+  if (!fixture_created)
+  {
+    /* Every statement below is written for the temporary tables; without
+     * them it would reach the permanent ones. */
+    conn = saved_conn;
+    mysql_available = saved_available;
+    mysql_close(connection);
+    CuAssertTrue(tc, live_tables_migrated);
+    CuFail(tc, "could not create the legacy pet fixture");
+    return;
+  }
+  first_migration = run_pet_persistence_migrations();
```

Checked with this patch on head: in all three states the test still fails and the row keeps `owner_id` 7; on a fresh database the test passes twice in a row. The patch also covers a fixture that fails part-way, which base did not.

What the patch leaves: of two processes started together on a never-migrated database, one still fails, because the runner checks a version and records it in separate statements. The live-schema test has had that property since before this MR; with the patch it costs a rerun and writes nothing outside the migrations.

**Finding 2 (the guide now says the opposite of the code): `docs/guides/TESTING_GUIDE.md:526-535` still names one test that writes to the permanent pet tables**

**Location.** `docs/guides/TESTING_GUIDE.md:526-535`, not touched by this MR; made false by `b06a2367f` (`unittests/CuTest/test_database_persistence.c:832`).

The paragraph reads: "Most pet persistence tests also isolate themselves with temporary tables. The exception is `Test_pet_live_schema_cascades_objects_and_rejects_orphans` ...". After this MR `Test_pet_persistence_legacy_schema_migration_is_idempotent` is a second exception: before it creates its temporary tables it runs the migration runner on the permanent `pet_data` and `pet_save_objs`, which is DDL, the `2026091005` orphan purge, and fifteen rows in the permanent `schema_migrations`.

The paragraph also ends "the booted suite applies migration `2026091007` for real on every fresh database and this test observes its outcome". That is the claim this MR removed from the fixture's comment because it does not hold when the boot is skipped.

This paragraph is where a reader learns which database tests leave the configured database changed, so it is the one place the change has to be recorded.

**Repro.** On a database built from `sql/master_schema.sql`, boot skipped, run the legacy test alone on head: the permanent `pet_save_objs` gains `fk_pet_save_objs_pet` and `schema_migrations` gains versions 2026080501 to 2026091007. On base the same run leaves both as they were. The guide describes base.

**Fix.** Replace the paragraph, for example:

```text
Most pet persistence tests also isolate themselves with temporary tables. Two
do not, because InnoDB refuses foreign keys on temporary tables and the
validator reads the key from `information_schema`:
`Test_pet_live_schema_cascades_objects_and_rejects_orphans` and
`Test_pet_persistence_legacy_schema_migration_is_idempotent`. Both run the
migration runner on the live `pet_data` and `pet_save_objs` tables from
`sql/master_schema.sql` and leave them migrated. The first then checks the
cascade and orphan rejection inside a transaction that is rolled back; the
second builds its legacy fixture in temporary tables. CI loads the master
schema into its isolated database before the suite runs; the master schema
carries no foreign key, so whichever runs first on a fresh database (the
syntax-check boot or one of these two tests) applies migration `2026091007`
for real.
```

**Review of `115b6d846` against base `8c0c5bd16`: two findings, one thread each.**

1. Data loss on a failure path: when the new permanent-table migration fails, the test's unguarded `UPDATE pet_data SET owner_id = 4294967295` lands on the permanent table. Reproduced three ways; patch given and checked. Thread on `test_database_persistence.c:833`.
2. `docs/guides/TESTING_GUIDE.md:526-535` still says one pet test writes to the permanent tables; this MR makes it two. Replacement text given.

Finding 1 should be fixed before merge. Nothing else was found in the two commits.

Run during the review, on head, against a disposable database built from `sql/master_schema.sql` with the boot skipped:

- The cause named in the description holds: on base the test passes with the key added by hand and fails without it.
- The test alone passes on mariadb:10.11 and on mariadb:11.4; so do its two neighbours on 11.4. On 11.4 `information_schema.TABLES` lists the temporary table too, but the foreign-key lookup still returns the permanent table's key.
- Each of the 36 tests in `test_database_persistence.c` passes alone on its own fresh database.
- `./cutest` with the database tests on, first run on a fresh database: 2039 of 2039.
- On an empty database the test fails at `:873` as the description says, and leaves a permanent `schema_migrations` behind.

added 3 commits
  • bf3ad8c3 - Keep the pet legacy-migration test's write off the permanent pet_data
  • f879086e - Name both pet tests that migrate the permanent tables in the testing guide
  • 4fe9a1c5 - Record the review of phase 2: two findings, both fixed
[Compare with previous version](/max757/Luminari-Source/-/merge_requests/24/diffs?diff_id=2077788224&start_sha=115b6d846fa19396c0c4c5880002b59d2c1c5fb9)

Confirmed, and fixed in `bf3ad8c39`.

**Reproduced on `115b6d846`.** mariadb:10.11, database from `sql/master_schema.sql`, boot skipped, one pet row with `owner_id` 7. All three states end with `Realowner 4294967295`, with the errors in the table above; the two-process state did so in 3 of 3 rounds. A fourth state ends the same way on head, and by the code on base too: a user with every right except CREATE TEMPORARY TABLES, where the migration run succeeds and the fixture cannot be created.

**Fix.** The statement runs only when the fixture was created:

```c
  /* Without the fixture this name is the permanent table, which the test must not write. */
  max_owner_id_rows =
      fixture_created && mysql_query(connection, "UPDATE pet_data SET owner_id = 4294967295") == 0
```

This is narrower than the patch above, on purpose. The `UPDATE` is the only write below that point: the other statements are `SELECT COUNT(*)`, and the second `run_pet_persistence_migrations()` waits for `first_migration`, which waits for `fixture_created`. The fifteen migrations alter, update and delete but never drop or rename a table, so once the fixture exists the name is the temporary table to the end of the test. A guard on the one statement keeps the test's single teardown and its `&&` chain; stopping the test there would repeat the teardown at a second exit.

**Checked on the pushed head** (the test file is the one of `bf3ad8c39`), same setup:

| State | Test | Row after |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Fresh database | passes, and again on the same database | `owner_id` 7 |
| Key added by hand, nothing recorded | fails at `:874`, `live_tables_migrated` | 7 |
| User with SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE TEMPORARY TABLES | fails at `:874` | 7 |
| Two processes started together, 3 rounds | each round one fails at `:874` and the other passes; a rerun passes | 7 |
| User without CREATE TEMPORARY TABLES | fails at `:875`, `fixture_created` | 7 |

No test covers the failure path: reaching it takes a second database user or a hand-altered permanent schema, and the suite has one configured user.

What stays, as the finding says: of two processes started together on a database that has not been migrated, one fails. It writes nothing outside the migrations and passes when run again. Every CI job has a database of its own; the testing guide now says not to start two suites that way (`f879086e4`, finding 2).

Confirmed, and fixed in `f879086e4`.

On head the legacy test alone, on a `master_schema.sql`-only database with the boot skipped, leaves `fk_pet_save_objs_pet` on the permanent `pet_save_objs` and the fifteen versions in the permanent `schema_migrations`. The guide described base.

The paragraph is the proposed text with two additions:

- Both tests "leave them migrated, as a server boot does".
- A last sentence for what finding 1 leaves: "Do not start two suites at once on a database that has not been migrated: the runner checks a version and records it in separate statements, so one of them fails and passes when run again."

**Both review findings are confirmed and fixed. Head is `4fe9a1c56`; the tag `object-save-fixes-p2` stays on `115b6d846`.**

1. Data loss on a failure path: fixed in `bf3ad8c39`. The `UPDATE` runs only when the temporary fixture was created. It is the one write below that point, so the fix is a guard on that statement, not the early return proposed in the thread; the thread has the reasoning and the table of states. In every failure state the test still fails and the permanent row keeps its `owner_id`.
2. Testing guide: fixed in `f879086e4`. Both tests are named, and the paragraph says not to start two suites at once on a database that has not been migrated.

`4fe9a1c56` records the review in the plan.

Run on `f879086e4`:

- `make -j16 test`: 2039 tests pass.
- `./cutest` with the database tests on, first run on a fresh `master_schema.sql`-only database: 2039 of 2039.
- `python3 scripts/ci/local/run.py --base gitlab/master`: 33 of 33 jobs pass (266 s). The format, hygiene and secrets jobs pass again on `4fe9a1c56`.

Both threads are resolved. Ready to merge: merge commit, no squash, as the plan's step 6 says.
